test_title: PYST 5: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 13th_September_2025_Shift_2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following correctly reflects the legal implication of Article 255 regarding presidential or governor's assent to bills?

options.text: State law is void without written Governor assent.
Mention of assent is mandatory for validity.
Omission of prior recommendation doesn't invalidate law if assent is given.
President's assent must precede legislative passage to be valid.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Omission of prior recommendation doesn't invalidate law if assent is given**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 255 of the Indian Constitution states that the absence of prior recommendation or sanction required by the Constitution does not invalidate a law if it has received the assent of the President or the Governor.
 
• The provision ensures that minor procedural lapses do not obstruct the legislative process, provided the bill has been duly assented to.
 
• For example, even if a recommendation from the President or Governor is not obtained at the time of introducing a bill, the law remains valid if subsequent assent is granted.
 
• This article upholds the principle of legislative supremacy by ensuring that procedural errors do not nullify valid legislative acts.
 
• It applies to both state and central legislation, ensuring uniformity in the treatment of procedural lapses related to assent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Constitutional Articles (Part VI, Chapter II)**

 
 
• Article 153: Establishes the office of the Governor for each state (one person can be Governor for two or more states).
 
• Article 154: Vests the executive power of the state in the Governor.
 
• Article 155: Appointment by the President (warrant under hand and seal).
 
• Article 156: Term of office (holds office during President's pleasure).
 
• Article 157: Qualifications for appointment (Citizen of India, 35 years old).
 
• Article 163: Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor (except in discretionary matters).
 
• Article 164: Other provisions as to Ministers (appointment, responsibility to the Assembly).
